newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - March 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation reported a a 26 per cent rise in net profit due to the rapid development of businesses outside Hong Kong.
-- SING TAO -- Pro-Beijing businessman Henry Fok criticised the Hong Kong Government for pushing property prices high and leaving the burden to the SAR government.

-- WEN WEI PO -- At the conference of the National People's Congress Chinese leaders expressed hopes of solving the problems of loss-making state enterprises in three years, so that they could play a bigger role in China's economy.
-- Chinese Vice Premier Zhu Rongji said central government would spend 30 billion yuan to reform state enterprises.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese Premier Li Peng said the Hong Kong handover was an important event to all Chinese, and firework displays would be put on throughout the country on the handover day.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Veteran pro-Beijing businessman Henry Fok fiercely attacked Hong Kong democrats in Beijing, saying that the SAR government should be alert to the destructive effect of protests.
-- Red-chip China Aerospace Internatinal Holdings tapped the stock market, placing $546.8 million worth of shares.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD --Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa is considering forming a special task force on housing.

-- China is turning away from setting communist-style output targets for its steel industry and stressing marketability. The metallurgy ministry had set a modest target this year of 100 million tonnes to encourage the industry to focus on quality.
